transcript:
Meeting Header:
Date: 2025-11-05
Time: 14:00 UTC (52m)
Duration: 00:52:00
Attendees: Ethan Kim, Laura Chen, Diego Ramos (Redwood); Priya Singh, Martin Lowe, Jasmeen Patel (Sable Health)
Shared resources: partner-playbook-v3.pdf (link), lead-routing-template.xlsx (link), bench-plan-draft.md (link)

[00:00] Ethan: hey everyone thanks for jumping on, um I think we have about 50 minutes so we'll go through the partner pipeline scrub and then pick the top accounts to move into co-sell. quick check on agenda — is that good?
[00:12] Martin: yep that works — we mostly want to make sure we know who owns outreach and avoid duplicate touches, also curious about the pilot flow.
[00:20] Laura: cool, i'll flag any technical blockers early, we might need to book a longer deep dive after this.
[00:30] Diego: quick note — i'll be tracking attribution rules and referral splits, so want to agree on lead routing today for EMEA and NA.
[00:38] Priya: perfect, we also have some SOC two questions — um sorry Sock two — and encryption/KMS concerns for our clinical data.
[00:46] Ethan: sure, Diego and Laura will outline those later. ok first section: pipeline scrub — i've pulled the partner-sourced deals from the sheet, there's ~28 live opps, i've pre-filtered to 12 that meet our ARR threshold and are in target ICP.
[01:05] Martin: can you share the filter? like what was the ARR threshold and tech fit?
[01:10] Ethan: i used >$75k ACV and latency-sensitive workloads or regulatory needs (healthcare/finserv), excluded pure R&D POCs unless they had procurement buy-in.
[01:20] Priya: that sounds fair. can we flag which ones require private deployment or V-P-C connectivity? we can't put PHI on a hosted API for a couple of accounts.
[01:31] Laura: yes — in the sheet i marked "Private needed" when they require VPC/V-P-C or on-prem. note: some of those can run in Redwood Dedicated with customer-managed network.
[01:43] Ethan: ok we have 4 accounts flagged Private. let's go through the top 8 and call priority 1/2/3.

[02:00] (list review, transcript compresses repeated account names)
[03:20] Ethan: Account A — large payer, legal expects SOC2 + audit logs and third-party attestations, Priya is that a blocker?
[03:28] Priya: they require SOC2 type II and proof of KMS integration — they also want signed BAA. we can engage procurement but need answers fast.
[03:36] Laura: Redwood has SOC2 and we can integrate KMS through our private deployment's HSM or cloud KMS — i can send the security brief. note: sometimes the transcription misses a term, but the doc is up to date.
[03:49] Jasmeen: send the security brief and the SOC2 cert, please.
[03:52] Ethan: will do. next — Account B looks high priority; partner already has an intro but no call scheduled. who owns outreach?
[04:02] Martin: Sable can intro, but we'd prefer Redwood takes lead for the technical contact.
[04:08] Diego: suggestion — Redwood AE owns initial technical intro for co-sell deals, partner handles executive warm intro. that keeps messages aligned.
[04:18] Ethan: agreed. add to next steps: i will send joint intro email templates.

[04:30] Laura: moving to bench/pilot criteria — we proposed a 2-week technical bench that measures latency P50/P95, token cost, and semantic fit on a standard prompt set. wanting to confirm metrics with Priya.
[04:46] Priya: that sounds reasonable, add privacy checklist — we cannot include production PHI, so provide synthetic datasets or redacted sample data.
[04:55] Laura: yes we can do synthetic. the bench will include: latency (P50/P95), throughput (requests/s), cost per 1k tokens, and sample quality evals with 20 prompts.
[05:06] Ethan: also include a failure-mode test — see how fallback to a smaller model affects latency and cost. that matters if we need graceful degradation in production.
[05:16] Martin: okay — what about competitors? Anthropic and Bedrock are in a lot of their RFIs. how do we position?
[05:25] Ethan: emphasize control of serving and cost levers — dedicated pools and quantization profiles. We also call out unified runtime across hosted, dedicated, private — fewer changes for their engineering teams when we switch hosting.
[05:40] Priya: procurement always asks about vendor lock-in. how does co-sell messaging handle that?
[05:46] Diego: co-sell playbook will have an "exit/portability" section: model versioning, export of weights (where allowed), and standard APIs to reduce lock-in risk.

[06:00] (brief cross-talk)
[06:12] Ethan: pricing ops — do we give partner credit for ARR or for first-year revenue? Diego?
[06:17] Diego: opt for partner credit on net new ARR for the first 12 months, with slotted attribution if multiple partners touch the account. we'll detail in the lead-routing sheet.
[06:26] Martin: also want a simple view for sales — who to credit if deal closes within 90 days of partner intro.
[06:31] Diego: yes, 90-day escrow rule is typical. i'll add examples.

[06:40] Laura: technical risk triage — a few accounts need on-prem or HSM integration. the biggest unknown is infra maturity on their side, e.g., k8s version, GPU availability. we should schedule a SE call early.
[06:55] Priya: we can prepare their infra team; they are small but can spin up a test env.
[07:03] Ethan: let's pick the top 5 to push to co-sell this quarter: Account B, Account C, Account D, Account E, Account A (private). Any objections?
[07:15] Martin: lists sounds right. B and C have executive interest. D is a stretch but partner warm intro is good.
[07:22] Priya: agree. Jasmeen will run legal prelims on A and D.

[07:33] Ethan: ok outreach ownership — Redwood AE will own technical outreach and initial demo; partner will own executive relationships and intro. Diego will define routing.
[07:43] Diego: i'll share the lead-routing-template with columns: account, partner, redwood rep, attribution rule, last-touch, evidence link.
[07:53] Ethan: next — marketing/co-marketing assets: we have a joint logo placement ask — do you want a joint press release for wins?
[08:00] Martin: yes for wins >$200k ARR. smaller deals can get a case study later.
[08:06] Ethan: noted.

[08:12] (Discussion about sales cadence and partner incentives)
[09:10] Priya: question about SSO and RBAC — can we map to Sable's SAML provider?
[09:16] Laura: yes with private deployment we can integrate SAML/SSO and fine-grained RBAC. but hosted API also supports SSO for the console. i'll post the SSO integration doc.
[09:28] Priya: great.

[09:34] Ethan: any major commercial blockers from your side? Jasmeen?
[09:39] Jasmeen: timeline — we typically run procurement cycles over 6–8 weeks for larger contracts. need clear documentation on SLAs and data handling.
[09:47] Ethan: we'll prioritize the security & SLA docs.

[09:53] (Pause — shuffling papers)
[10:05] Laura: technical detail — for the bench i propose we run three model configurations: hosted standard, dedicated quantized, and private full precision. that shows tradeoffs in latency/cost/quality.
[10:20] Martin: good, can we highlight which configuration meets compliance?
[10:24] Laura: private full precision and dedicated with VPC can meet compliance; hosted is less likely for PHI.

[10:33] Ethan: ok — on the joint outreach timeline: initial email templates by Friday, intro calls scheduled next week for B and C, bench kickoff week after. does that timeline work?
[10:45] Priya: yes please include our legal contact on the security thread.
[10:50] Diego: will do.

[11:00] (Wrap-up and recap)
[11:05] Ethan: recap: top 5 accounts moved to co-sell; Redwood AE owns technical outreach; Diego owns routing sheet; Laura owns bench plan; Priya/Jasmeen will run procurement/security checks for accounts A and D. deliverables and due dates in next steps.
[11:24] Martin: sounds good. did we agree a follow-up meeting cadence?
[11:29] Ethan: weekly 30-min sync for next 6 weeks to move deals; i'll send an invite.
[11:35] Priya: ok thanks everyone.
[11:38] Jasmeen: thanks.
[11:40] (call ends)

Notes on transcription quirks: occasional mis-hearings e.g., "K-V cash" for "KV cache", "Sock two" for SOC2, and some names may be abbreviated. Action items and links captured above.
